mapping_algorithm.step_1: For each MB104 node P_i, evaluate incidence with the 35 retained known-curve basis classes indexed by INDLIST <= 92, using the exact Stoll/Testa curve equations and the exact MB104 Q(i) node coordinates.
mapping_algorithm.step_2: From the retained Picard64 Gram matrix, extract for each of the 29 retained exceptional basis classes its pairing row against the same 35 retained curve basis classes.
mapping_algorithm.step_3: Match the two exact 35-entry incidence fingerprints. This recovers retained exceptional labels to MB104 node labels without using or guessing Magma's singular-point enumeration order.
mapping_algorithm.step_4: For every MB104 exceptional E_i, form its 64 selected pairings: -2 against its own retained exceptional basis class when present, 0 against the other retained exceptionals, and its exact 35 curve incidences. Reconstruct its primitive retained Picard64 vector with RetainedBasisPairingTransform.
mapping_algorithm.step_5: Form K_res=-E24+E25-E26+E27-E32+E33-E34+E35 and verify K_res^2=-16 in the retained Gram lattice before any transport claim.
mapping_algorithm.step_6: Because selected=P*Gram is a row permutation of the retained primitive Gram basis, the coefficient row of ell_res(v)=<v,K_res> on selected pairing coordinates is exactly P*x_Kres, where x_Kres is the primitive Picard64 coordinate vector.
mapping_algorithm.step_7: Split that exact 64-coordinate functional into the HPADJ 11 fixed selected pairings and 53 free selected pairings. Free part zero means terminal-visible on the certified HPADJ interface scope; nonzero free part routes to BR103 exact congruence-aware cancellation/minimization.
